newsitem.title: YEMEN: Too soon to decide on British Zaire role - Rifkind.
newsitem.headline: Too soon to decide on British Zaire role - Rifkind.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Wednesday it was too early to say if British troops would join a multilateral force for Zaire proposed by French President Jacques Chirac.
"I think we will want to look over it carefully," Rifkind told reporters in the Yemeni capital Sanaa when asked if Britain was in favour of such a force.

Asked if he could foresee British troops joining the force, he said: "I think it is far too early to express an opinion on that. The French have put out a general proposal in general terms and we and all other countries concerned are waiting to clarify with our French colleagues what they have in mind and also to see what is happening on the ground."

"I don't want to speculate about that at this stage frankly. There are always problems if you send troops to any part of the world where there are serious difficulties. We have to see what is the best way of easing the situation," he added.
Rifkind had said on Tuesday Britain would discuss the proposed force at a summit meeting in France on Friday.

France is championing a military intervention in eastern Zaire to save the lives of the refugees, mainly Hutus who fled Rwanda two years ago after the Hutu genocide of up to one million Tutsis and other victims in their homeland.
African leaders held their first summit on the war in eastern Zaire on Tuesday as 1.2 million refugees in the region faced a growing threat of famine.
Zaire boycotted the Nairobi summit, dimming hopes of any diplomatic way out of the impasse -- how to reach the refugees and avert catastrophe.
